changes.1.2: adds input.key, input.joystick, display.set_monitor, screen.render, audio.*, tape.*, disc.info, disc.export, rom.unload and the debug.* group, so a frontend (the WASM web app) can drive the whole machine through CPCApi; run.frames also reports ran and break; disc.load takes an optional name; machine.reset clears a debugger stop
changes.1.1: state.save/state.restore use the canonical state format 1 (identical bytes on every build and ABI; earlier build-specific images are rejected); state.hash is FNV-1a 64 of that canonical stream plus disc CRCs and ROM bytes, so its values differ from 1.0; session.capabilities reports state_format

protocol: JSON-RPC 2.0 over one-request-per-line stdio (a request line may not exceed 1 MiB, so with base64 a disc or snapshot is limited to about 780 KB over stdio); string values follow RFC 8259 escapes including \uXXXX and surrogate pairs; \u0000 is refused; replies are always valid UTF-8 JSON (a byte sequence that is not UTF-8, such as a Latin-1 symbol, comes back as U+FFFD); debugger expressions nest at most 64 levels; state-changing integer parameters (symbol value, ids, pass_count, values written) must be integers or the call fails, they are never defaulted

rom.unload.result: boolean; the role is empty again (roms_loaded reports it)

result.ran: frames run by this call (fewer than count when a debugger stop ended it)
result.break: boolean, true when a breakpoint, run-to, step-out or BRK stopped the machine (debug.step_into never sets it); clear it with debug.resume

result.advanced_nops: integer (can overshoot at an instruction boundary)

cpu.registers.result: primary and alternate Z80 registers, interrupt state, halt state and virtual counters

params.name: optional display name kept with the disc (default <api>)

result.name: string
result.data_base64: the disc as a DSK image, including writes the machine made

params.metadata: optional boolean; when true also return screen_mode, CRTC type/registers, hardware palette indices, and current ARGB palette

result.data_base64: explicit RGBA bytes in row-major order
result.metadata: optional when requested: screen_mode, crtc_type, crtc_registers, palette_hw and palette_argb

result.hash: 16 lowercase hexadecimal digits: FNV-1a 64 of the canonical state stream, then mounted disc CRCs and loaded ROM bytes; equal on every build

result.data_base64: exact machine state, canonical format 1: loads in any build (handoff between instances)

params.data_base64: canonical state from state.save of any build; malformed input is rejected without changing the machine

params.mask: active-low byte; zero bits are pressed

params.key: matrix position row * 8 + bit, row 0..9 (cpc_keys.h CPC_KEY)

params.bit: 0..7 (up, down, left, right, fire1, fire2, fire3)

display.set_monitor.result: boolean; configuration only (not machine state). It recolours Plus machines; the CPC 6128 palette ignores it

params.pal: boolean, default true: PAL horizontal blend
params.scanlines: boolean, default true: draw the second line of each pair (half brightness when pal is true, an exact copy when pal is false); false leaves it black

result.data_base64: presentation image, what the web canvas shows

params.frames: optional, default everything queued, at most 8192 per call

params.data_base64: CDT, TZX, VOC, WAV or CSV image
params.name: optional, default tape.cdt

tape.play.result: boolean; error when no tape is loaded (web/bridge.c made this a no-op)

tape.rewind.result: boolean; error when no tape is loaded

debug.attach.result: debug.status; attaches the debugger and enables breakpoints (symbols.load leaves them off)

debug.detach.result: debug.status; drops breakpoints, symbols and data areas

result.attached: boolean; methods that change debugger state, debug.disassemble and symbolic addresses (a name in any address parameter) attach it, read-only debug.* calls and unknown methods do not
result.history: boolean, the execution history ring; always false after any API call
result.break_index: breakpoint id, -1 for step/run-to/step-out, -2 for BRK

debug.resume.result: boolean; clears the stop so the next run.* continues

debug.pause.result: boolean; cancels a pending run-to or step-out

result.pc: integer after executing one instruction (a HALT is completed)

debug.step_out.result: boolean; arms a stop after the current routine returns, run.* then advances

debug.run_to.result: boolean; arms a stop at the address, run.* then advances

debug.symbols.set.result: boolean; value is required; error when 16384 symbols exist (updating an existing name still works; symbols.load is not capped)

debug.data.mark.result: boolean; the disassembly shows the range as data

result.instructions: [{address, length, text}] honouring symbols and data areas

result.hex: bytes as seen through the current paging

debug.mem.write.result: boolean; writes through the current paging

result.breakpoints: [{id, type: code|mem_read|mem_write|io|change, enabled, start, end, pass_count, hits, condition}]

result.set: boolean, whether a code breakpoint exists there now

result.ids: every breakpoint created: readwrite makes two (read, write); all or nothing, an error when the table (256) cannot hold them

params.condition: debugger expression, empty for none; at most 159 bytes (longer is an error, never truncated)

result.error: why the expression was rejected, empty when set

clock: Virtual only: it advances on run.* calls. One NOP is 4 T-states; instruction steps cannot stop mid-instruction, so run.nops may advance past its requested count. t_states_aligned is NOP-aligned.
